Hi Priya / Samir — attaching the short workbook and a one-page pricing snapshot to illustrate the three deployment economics. High level notes below: 

Attachment: velox_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 46 KB)
Attachment: redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf (pdf, 18 KB)

Summary (assumptions in workbook):
- Workload: 2k peak QPS, token mix per Priya's note (60/30/10). We modeled 30-day and 90-day smoothing for capacity.

Hosted API (per-token):
- Pros: fastest to start, no infra ops, pay-as-you-go for variable traffic.
- Cons: per-token unit costs higher under sustained high QPS.
- Example: estimated $0.018 / 1K tokens effective for your mix -> monthly ~$32k for baseline traffic (subject to burst and streaming usage).

Dedicated capacity (reserved commits):
- Pros: predictable throughput, lower per-token equivalent cost when fully utilized, data isolation within tenant pool.
- Cons: requires commit (monthly/annual), needs sizing & headroom for peaks.
- Example: 4x A100-equivalent reserved pool (autoscaling buffer) -> commit ~$45k/mo with effective per-token ~$0.008 when utilization >70%. Break-even vs Hosted at ~60% sustained utilization.

Private VPC / On-prem:
- Pros: full control, meets hardest security/compliance needs (bring-your-KMS), suitable for regulated customers.
- Cons: license + support + infra capex/opex; longer procurement cycle.
- Pricing: one-time platform license + annual support + optional dedicated operator add-on. We included a starter example in the workbook (estimated first-year TCO ~ $300–450k depending on infra choices).

Next steps I suggest:
- Quick 30-min review to walk the workbook (I can run numbers for different commit sizes).
- Aditya / Priya: confirm if a 3-month pilot with a lower commit (e.g., $25k/mo) would be acceptable as a ramp path to full Dedicated. That lets you prove economics before annualizing.

I'll be available Tue 11/24 10:00–12:00 PT and Wed 11/25 14:00–16:00 PT for the walkthrough — send over preferred slot and I'll calendar it.

— Marissa
